references.text: Abraham and Abimelek swore an oath to each other at Be'er-Sheva. The place name Be'er-Sheva is linked here to an oath, just as Isaac in 26:33 names the well Shiv'a after making an oath with Abimelek.
Abraham names Be'er-Sheva and plants a tamarisk there, showing the site's early significance as a place for covenants and worship—a tradition that Isaac continues in chapter 26.
After the binding of Isaac, Abraham returns to Be'er-Sheva and settles there, highlighting the central role this place played for the patriarchs.
Isaac and Abimelek swear an oath to each other—the direct reason why Isaac names the well Shiv'a (oath) in verse 33.
Be'er-Sheva is assigned to the tribe of Simeon as part of their inheritance, showing the site's continued importance in Israel's history.
